neighbours.label: the particle 'in' completing 'drop in' / 'drop-in' (an informal visit), as opposed to 'drop' with other particles and 'in' after other verbs
fire: If you are passing by, just drop in and say hello.
The clinic offers drop-in hours every Tuesday afternoon.
My cousin dropped in last night with a box of cakes.
Parents are welcome to drop in during the art class.
The centre runs a drop-in group for new mothers.
We might drop in on the Smiths after the market.
Neighbours kept dropping in all afternoon to see the baby.
Students can drop in at the writing lab without an appointment.
quiet: If you are passing by, just stop and say hello.
The clinic offers walk-up hours every Tuesday afternoon.
My cousin dropped off a box of cakes last night.
Parents are welcome to sit in during the art class.
The centre runs a weekly group for new mothers.
We might drop by the Smiths' house after the market.
Neighbours kept coming over all afternoon to see the baby.
Students can visit the writing lab without an appointment.
